en: O you who ride upon a mouse, who hold a sweetmeat in your hand, whose ears are adorned with hanging threads, who possess a dwarf form, son of Maheśvara, Vighnavināyaka—homage to your feet!
To the god who is the son of the God of gods, the remover of obstacles for the world, who has the form of an elephant, a massive body, and a radiance equal to ten million suns; || 1 ||
He was a dwarf with matted hair, lovely yet short-necked and pot-bellied; his cheeks were smeared with grey ash and vermilion, and he was formidable, manifesting a fierce majesty.
He has a single tusk and protruding lips; he wears a serpent as a sacred thread; he is three-eyed and elephant-faced; he is dark-complexioned, auspicious, and clothed in red garments.
I bow to the holy and divine Gaṇapati, the King of Obstacles, who holds a tusk in his hand, who grants boons, who is devoted to Brahman, and who is a celibate student. || 4 ||
To the god Gaṇapati, the Lord who goes before the universe, the one superior to and most excellent among the gods, the leader, the great Vināyaka. || 5 ||
I bow to the Blessed One, the God, the wondrous Leader of the Gaṇas; salutations to you, Vakratuṇḍa, the fierce one, with the formidable face.
Salutations to you, the fierce one, the exceedingly fierce one, and the most fiercely fierce; salutations to you, who are intoxicated, mad, and heedless, and who are eternally intoxicated. || 7 ||
I bow to the son of Umā; salutations to you, the son of Gaṅgā. Salutations to you, who are Oṃkāra, Vaṣaṭkāra, and Svāhākāra. || 8 ||
O you whose form is mantra, O great yogin, O Jātavedas, salutations again and again! Salutations to you who hold an axe and a noose in your hands, and who possess the trunk of an elephant! 9.
Salutations again and again to Megha, to Meghavarṇa, and to Megheśvara; salutations to you, the terrible one, of terrible form, and more terrible than the terrible. || 10 ||
Salutations again and again to the Primordial Person, the one worshipped by the ancients; O Madotkaṭa, salutations to you; and salutations to you, O Caṇḍavikrama.
O Vināyaka, homage be unto you; homage be unto you, O you who are affectionate toward your devotees! Homage to the one dear to his devotees, the peaceful one, the possessor of great splendor. 12.

Salutations again and again to the sacrifice, to the priest of the sacrifice, and to the Lord of the sacrifice; salutations to You whose limbs are smeared with white ashes and who wear white garlands.
Salutation to the Lord of the Gaṇas, whose cheeks are moistened by intoxication; salutation to him who is fond of red flowers and adorned with red sandalwood paste. 14.
Salutations to you, the peaceful Agnihotra, who is unconquerable; salutations to you, O Lord of Gods, who has a rat for a vehicle and possesses a single tusk. || 15 ||
Salutations to you, the heroic Śūrpakarṇa with long tusks; may Vināyaka, the son of Śiva and lord of gods, remove all obstacles. || 16 ||

From the recitation of this very [mantra], from its oblation, and likewise from the twilight worship, one obtains the fruit [of these rites]: a Brahmin becomes rich in the Vedas, and a Kshatriya becomes victorious.
The Vaiśya shall become enriched with wealth, and the Śūdra is liberated from sins; a pregnant woman shall give birth to a son, and a maiden shall obtain a husband.
The traveler finds a place to stay; the bound is released from bondage; one attains the fulfillment of desires and purifies even the most degraded lineage.
It is the most auspicious of all auspicious things, the destroyer of all sins, and the bestower of all desires upon men who recite it or even hear it.
Thus ends the hymn to Vināyaka, proclaimed by Skanda, within the glorious Brahmāṇḍa Purāṇa.
